title: Stator
model_title: Induction Motor Stator: Frame, Laminated Core, Three-Phase Windings & Terminal Box

introduction.definition: The stator is the stationary part of an induction motor: a frame holding a laminated, slotted core in which three-phase windings are laid. Currents 120° apart in the three windings create a magnetic field that rotates at synchronous speed and drives the rotor.
applications: Induction motors for all industrial drives
introduction.summary: An induction-motor stator is the stationary part: a frame holding a laminated core whose slots carry three-phase windings. Three-phase current in the windings produces a magnetic field that rotates at synchronous speed.

magnetic_field.title: Three phase currents make a rotating field
magnetic_field.description: Three windings 120° apart carry currents 120° out of phase; their combined field rotates at synchronous speed n_s = 120·f / p (e.g. 1500 rpm for 4 poles at 50 Hz). The laminated core carries the flux with low eddy-current loss. Winding insulation (class F/H) is the life-limiting part: each ≈ 10 °C over its rating roughly halves insulation life, so overload, poor cooling and voltage unbalance matter. Test with insulation resistance / polarisation index.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Stator.
Check winding temperature and currents.
Insulation resistance / PI test.
Clean, dry, varnish; rewind if needed.
Watch for insulation failure: earth fault trip. Common cause: overheating, moisture, contamination.
Watch for single phasing: hum, overheating. Common cause: lost phase.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
